paperTitle: O-Level Basic Band — Practice 07: The Wrong Bus
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band. Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Short passage (~230 words, everyday vocabulary), 2 short-answer + 3 MCQ. Most marks reachable by choosing — typed items run a 64% blank rate in the weakest cohort.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
My grandmother came to stay with us in December. She had not been to Singapore for eleven years.

Paragraph 2
On her third day she went out alone to buy fish. She did not tell anyone.

Paragraph 3
At six o'clock she was still not back. My mother called the police. I went down to the bus stop to wait.

Paragraph 4
She came home at half past seven in a taxi. Her bag was empty. She had bought no fish.

Paragraph 5
She had taken bus 154 instead of bus 145. The numbers looked the same to her. The bus went the other way, past places she did not know.

Paragraph 6
She did not have a phone. She could not remember our address, only that our block was near a big tree.

Paragraph 7
A young woman on the bus noticed her crying. She sat with my grandmother for forty minutes, showed her photographs of trees on her phone, and found the right block. Then she paid for the taxi and would not take the money back.

Paragraph 8
My grandmother tells this story to everyone. She never mentions being lost. She only talks about the girl on the bus.

questions.stem: Q1. From Paragraph 2, why did the grandmother go out? [1]
Q2. From Paragraph 5, which bus should she have taken? [1]

questions.stem: Q3. Why did the grandmother take the wrong bus? [1]

options.text: The two numbers looked alike to her.
The bus stop had been moved.

questions.stem: Q4. In Paragraph 7, how did the young woman work out where the grandmother lived? [1]

options.text: She used photographs of trees to find the right block.
She took her to the police station.

questions.stem: Q5. In Paragraph 8, what does the grandmother's way of telling the story show? [1]

options.text: She has forgotten most of what happened.
She is angry with the bus company.
She wants people to remember the kindness, not her mistake.
She is proud of finding her own way home.
